{
  "skills": [
    {
      "skill_id": "inverted_solubility_lipophilicity_transfer",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "long_scaffold_hydrophobic_gain",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_long"},
          "weight": 0.55,
          "rationale": "Source ESOL effect for smiles_long was -11.46 on solubility; lipophilicity is the inverse partition axis, so sign flips positive."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "short_molecule_lipophilicity_penalty",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_short"},
          "weight": -0.6,
          "rationale": "Short SMILES raised solubility (+6.89) in source; small polar molecules partition poorly into octanol, so expect low logD."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "ring_dense_hydrophobic_core",
          "conditions": {"ring_token_bin": "ring_token_high"},
          "weight": 0.4,
          "rationale": "Ring role carried the largest transfer weight (0.758); fused ring surface lowers solubility and raises hydrophobic partitioning."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "branched_aliphatic_bulk",
          "conditions": {"branch_bin": "branch_high"},
          "weight": 0.22,
          "rationale": "Rotatable-bond to branch mapping transferred at 0.758; branched aliphatic bulk adds nonpolar surface area."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.0,
      "prior_scale": 0.35,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.45,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.15,
      "ucb_weight": 0.6,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.2,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.0,
      "gp_xi": 0.01,
      "confidence": 0.55,
      "hypothesis": "Transfers source solubility roles with inverted sign, assuming lipophilicity is the reciprocal partition axis. Fails if lipophilicity is driven by polarity composition rather than size, or if long SMILES are heteroatom-rich and polar."
    },
    {
      "skill_id": "polarity_halogen_partition_counter",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "low_heteroatom_nonpolar_core",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_low"},
          "weight": 0.6,
          "rationale": "Few heteroatoms means little hydrogen bonding or desolvation cost, the classical mechanistic driver of high octanol-water partitioning."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "heteroatom_rich_polar_penalty",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_high"},
          "weight": -0.45,
          "rationale": "Dense heteroatom substitution adds polar hydrogen-bond capacity, reducing lipophilicity despite large molecular size."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "halogen_rich_hydrophobic_substitution",
          "conditions": {"halogen_bin": "halogen_high"},
          "weight": 0.5,
          "rationale": "Halogenation increases polarizable nonpolar surface with negligible hydrogen bonding, a textbook additive logP increase."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "length_transfer_downweight",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_long"},
          "weight": -0.12,
          "rationale": "Counters the low-confidence (0.224) length role; long strings often encode polar heteroatom chains, not hydrophobic bulk."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.5,
      "prior_scale": 0.3,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.35,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.1,
      "ucb
